rule: Guard imports of optional cross-provider bases (e.g. BaseMessageQueueProvider) with a try/except that raises AirflowOptionalProviderFeatureException when the dependency is absent
trigger: A provider module imports from another optional provider package (e.g. airflow.providers.common.messaging, airflow.providers.openlineage) at module top-level without a try/except AirflowOptionalProviderFeatureException guard
rationale: Without the guard, importing the provider module crashes Airflow in environments where the optional provider is not installed; every other message-queue provider in the repo already follows this pattern

evidence.excerpt: importing this module doesn't crash Airflow in environments without that optional provider

rule: AssetWatcher triggers must use a while-True polling loop so the trigger never exits silently; a single await that can return None is not sufficient
trigger: A trigger's async run() method contains a single await call that can return None or raise, without an enclosing while True loop
rationale: If run() exits without yielding a TriggerEvent the AssetWatcher is silently killed and the DAG never triggers; Kafka's AwaitMessageTrigger uses while True as the established pattern

evidence.excerpt: trigger exits silently without yielding a TriggerEvent … kills the watcher and the DAG never triggers

rule: Do not mutate sys.modules in a provider test package __init__.py; use a pytest fixture (monkeypatch.setitem) scoped to the relevant tests instead
trigger: sys.modules["..."] = ... appears in a tests/ package __init__.py rather than inside a pytest fixture or conftest
rationale: Module-level sys.modules mutation is a global side effect that leaks into unrelated tests and masks missing-dependency behaviour across the test suite

evidence.excerpt: global side effect that can leak into unrelated tests and mask missing-dependency behavior

rule: Provider documentation examples targeting Airflow 3+ must use schedule= (not schedule_interval=) and import PythonOperator from airflow.providers.standard.operators.python
trigger: A provider README or docs example contains schedule_interval= or imports PythonOperator from airflow.operators.python when the provider's minimum Airflow version is 3
rationale: schedule_interval was removed in Airflow 3 and PythonOperator moved to the Standard provider; using legacy imports in docs contradicts the provider's declared Airflow 3+ requirement

evidence.excerpt: inconsistent with the provider's Airflow 3+ requirement … update to Airflow 3 style

rule: Use wait_for_completion (not wait_for_termination) as the boolean parameter name for operators that poll until a job/resource finishes, for consistency with the AWS provider convention
trigger: An operator __init__ declares a parameter named wait_for_termination
rationale: The AWS provider package already uses wait_for_completion universally; diverging names create an inconsistent user experience across providers

evidence.excerpt: We usually use wait_for_completion in the AWS provider package … use it as well for consistency

rule: Guard imports of BaseEventTrigger / TriggerEvent with an AIRFLOW_V_3_0_PLUS check and fall back to BaseTrigger for Airflow 2 compatibility
trigger: A provider trigger imports BaseEventTrigger or TriggerEvent from airflow.triggers.base unconditionally without an AIRFLOW_V_3_0_PLUS guard
rationale: BaseEventTrigger was introduced in Airflow 3; unconditional import breaks providers that must remain compatible with Airflow 2

evidence.excerpt: Adding compact import should fix the CI … AIRFLOW_V_3_0_PLUS guard

rule: An async (deferrable) hook must support the same connection extras as its synchronous counterpart; if an extra is unsupported, raise AirflowException explicitly rather than silently ignoring it
trigger: An async hook's credential-setup branch omits handling of connection extras (e.g. key_path, key_json) that the corresponding sync hook supports
rationale: Silent omission makes deferrable=True behave differently from the sync path for existing connections, breaking user workflows without a clear error

evidence.excerpt: async hook currently ignores them … make deferrable=True behave differently or fail for existing connections

rule: Tests for polling-retry loops must assert the sleep mock call count to verify the loop actually sleeps between polls
trigger: A test mocks time.sleep and tests a polling retry loop but does not assert mock_sleep.call_count
rationale: Without asserting sleep call count the test passes even if the implementation stops sleeping between polls, producing false positives

evidence.excerpt: avoid false positives if the implementation stops sleeping between polls

rule: In deferrable operators, do not use provisioning_state alone as a terminal-state signal for deferral decisions; only treat the container execution state as terminal
trigger: A deferrable operator checks cg_state.provisioning_state (e.g. 'Succeeded') as a condition to stop deferring, without also verifying instance_view.current_state
rationale: Provisioning can reach Succeeded while the container is still running and instance_view is not yet populated, causing premature exit from the deferral loop

evidence.excerpt: provisioning_state as a terminal state can prevent deferral … defer until container execution state is terminal

rule: When comparing cross-provider version strings use packaging.Version directly; do not wrap Version().base_version in another Version() call
trigger: Code contains Version(Version(...).base_version) when performing a cross-provider version comparison
rationale: packaging.Version already handles pre-release ordering correctly; the redundant base_version round-trip strips pre-release tags unnecessarily and adds confusion

evidence.excerpt: Version(Version(...).base_version) is redundant — packaging.Version already orders pre-release tags correctly

rule: The OpenLineage JDBC authority extractor must strip userinfo (user:pass@) from the URL and handle Oracle thin URLs that use @// instead of ://
trigger: A _get_openlineage_authority or equivalent JDBC URL parser splits on :// without also handling @// (Oracle thin) and does not strip user:pass@ from the result
rationale: Oracle thin JDBC URLs use jdbc:oracle:thin:@//host:port/service and many drivers allow embedding userinfo; missing these cases emits wrong or missing authority in OpenLineage events

evidence.excerpt: jdbc:oracle:thin:@//host doesn't contain :// … authority is lost for a perfectly parseable URL
user embeds userinfo in the JDBC URL … after ends up as user:pass@host:5432
